item.title: Xinhua think tank report highlights high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
XI'AN, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A national high-level think tank released a report on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy on Tuesday. The report, titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation," was released by Xinhua Institute, a think tank affiliated with Xinhua News Agency, at the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 & the 4th Silk Road (XI'AN) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, capital of northwest China's Shaanxi Province. Consisting of three chapters, the report showcases the concrete practices of Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) cooperation in building an open world economy, analyzes the serious challenges facing economic globalization, and explains the contemporary significance of BRI cooperation in following the historical trend and opening broad prospects for the world economy. According to the report, high-quality BRI cooperation exemplifies China's commitment to opening-up as a fundamental national policy and to a mutually beneficial opening-up strategy. The report noted that BRI cooperation has consistently upheld the principles of extensive consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits; embraced open, green, and clean cooperation; and pursued high standards, sustainability, and better lives for people. By steering economic globalization toward greater openness, inclusiveness, balance, and benefits for all, the BRI contributes Chinese approaches and insights to the building of an open world economy, it said. The report stated that the rise of anti-globalization sentiment, the spread of unilateralism and protectionism, weak global growth drivers, lagging governance, and uneven development are realities that must be confronted. At the same time, economic globalization reflects the objective requirements of the development of productive forces, and its historical direction cannot be reversed. Countries are more interdependent than ever, creating major opportunities to address global problems through openness and cooperation. Amid these changes, China's approach is to consider both domestic and international conditions, expand high-standard opening-up, and build global development partnerships. In this way, it seeks to turn challenges into a powerful impetus for an open world economy and realize a vision of inclusive development and mutual benefit for all, said the report. BRI cooperation keeps pace with the times, meets development needs, and responds to people's aspirations. It takes concrete action against decoupling, supply chain disruption, and bloc confrontation, using connectivity to remove barriers and facilitate economic flows, according to the report. At this new stage of history, BRI cooperation is moving from major corridors to extensive networks. Driven by digitalization and the green transition, it is deepening institutional opening-up and promoting collaborative innovation to make global development more balanced, inclusive, and sustainable, the report said. Looking ahead, the report stressed that BRI cooperation will provide stronger support for an open world economy, bring renewed vitality to global economic governance, reinforce the foundations of a community with a shared future for humanity, and open brighter prospects for world peace and development. The full report, comprising approximately 18,000 Chinese characters, was released globally in both Chinese and English through relevant websites, journals, social media, and other platforms. ■

item.title: Technological upgrading boosts slipper industry in E China's Cixi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
CIXI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Qiaotou Town of Cixi City is one of China's main production hubs for cotton slippers. For a long time, its cotton slipper industry was plagued by severe homogenization. Though the town ranked first nationwide in output of cotton slippers, its profits were slim. Since 2024, enterprises in Qiaotou Town have teamed up with College of Science and Technology Ningbo University and Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering of Chinese Academy of Sciences to improve quality of the slipper products through technological upgrading and R&D, and to cooperate in brand building, material R&D, and product design. Currently, the proportion of R&D expenses to operating revenue of 11 shoe enterprises above designated size in Qiaotou Town has risen from 1.31 percent in the same period of last year to 2.05 percent at present, and their R&D spending has kept growing over the past three years. In the first eight months of this year, the output value of the enterprises above designated size in the town's slipper industry climbed by 18.11 percent year on year.

item.title: China welcomes U.S. debut of new giant panda pair
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday he was delighted that a new pair of Chinese giant pandas have recently made their debut before the American public, bringing more joy to the American people. Guo made the comments at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on the public debut of a pair of Chinese giant pandas sent to the United States after Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the country in September. On Sept. 24, Xi announced during his visit that a pair of pandas would be sent to Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people. The pair, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, arrived on Sept. 27. Before meeting the public last week, they spent more than a month in quarantine, adjusting to the new bamboo, new caretakers and new environment. To ensure the giant pandas' health and safety, a smooth departure from China and their adaptation to the new environment, China and the United States have made full preparations in strict compliance with the requirements and technical standards for international giant panda conservation cooperation, according to Guo. "We believe the new round of cooperation will further contribute to enhancing the conservation capacity for giant pandas and other endangered species, advancing global biodiversity conservation, and deepening the friendship between the Chinese and American people," he said. ■

item.title: Xinhua Headlines: China's import expo tells a larger story of openness, shared opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
* The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors and featured more than 480 global, Asian or China debuts. Organizers reported 85.45 billion U.S. dollars in intended deals. * Greek financial news outlet Business Daily described the CIIE as an "importathon" -- a blend of "import" and "marathon," suggesting a sustained drive to bring goods into the Chinese market. * John Ross, a former director of economic and business policy for the mayor of London, told Xinhua that China was not seeking a trade surplus but rather greater openness in world trade. For foreign exporters, he called the CIIE "the best export opportunity that you've got in the world." SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- In 2018, German warehouse-equipment maker Jungheinrich showcased a German-made forklift at China's inaugural import expo. This year, it unveiled an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted warehouse-planning tool developed partly in China -- a sign of the country's growing role as a source of innovation for global businesses, not just a vast market. The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors and featured more than 480 global, Asian or China debuts. Organizers reported 85.45 billion U.S. dollars in intended deals. For decades, China's manufacturing strengths have drawn foreign companies, many of which have used the country as a base to serve global markets. In 2025, foreign-invested enterprises accounted for 27 percent of China's exports and 16 percent of its trade surplus, according to official figures. Shanghai has long been a major gateway for China's exports. In 2025, its port recorded total container throughput of more than 55 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), retaining its position as the world's busiest container port for the 16th consecutive year. The city has also become a gateway for foreign businesses seeking access to China's import market. Since 2018, it has hosted the CIIE, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, described by Chinese officials as "an international public good shared by the world." For Ethiopian economist Alemayehu Geda, China's expanding import market offers an opportunity for African producers to move beyond raw-material exports. China is "not only encouraging exporters as was traditionally the case, but also importers into China," the Addis Ababa University professor said. Greek financial news outlet Business Daily described the CIIE as an "importathon" -- a blend of "import" and "marathon," suggesting a sustained drive to bring goods into the Chinese market. Nepalese entrepreneur Shankar Koirala has witnessed those opportunities grow over six CIIE appearances. His booth expanded from nine to 72 square meters. Each handmade cashmere scarf bears its maker's signature. Together, the products connect Chinese buyers with more than 600 artisan families in Nepal. "When we didn't know where to promote our products, the CIIE gave us a platform," Koirala said. John Ross, a former director of economic and business policy for the mayor of London, told Xinhua that China was not seeking a trade surplus but rather greater openness in world trade. For foreign exporters, he called the CIIE "the best export opportunity that you've got in the world." China imported more than 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. At this year's CIIE, free exhibition space for the least developed countries increased by 17 percent, while the Asia-Africa products zone was upgraded. Beyond the exhibition halls, China has expanded preferential access to its market. Since May 1, eligible imports from all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations have enjoyed zero tariffs. That morning, 24 tonnes of South African apples became the first shipment cleared under the policy in Shenzhen. When China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, its annual goods trade stood at about 500 billion U.S. dollars. By 2025, it exceeded 6 trillion dollars. China's role as a buyer has grown as well: imports from more than 130 countries and regions increased last year, customs data showed. China has also taken steps in support of the multilateral trading system. In 2025, it announced it would not seek new special and differential treatment in current or future WTO negotiations. This year, it pledged 1.1 million dollars to WTO programs that support developing and least-developed economies. These efforts come as the multilateral trading system faces mounting challenges. The WTO's World Trade Report 2026 says global trade policy and the organization face "the most serious and sustained disruptions" since the multilateral trading system emerged 80 years ago. Addressing the opening ceremony of the CIIE, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called on countries to share market opportunities and promote balanced trade by making the economic pie bigger together. He also urged deeper investment cooperation, innovation and the removal of trade barriers. For French yeast maker Lesaffre, making that pie bigger through innovation can bring benefits well beyond China. At its Shanghai industrial baking center, the company tests processes for customers across Asia-Pacific. Solutions refined in China can be applied elsewhere, an approach the company calls the "China fulcrum effect." "A solution validated on these lines in China can be scaled for customers across Asia-Pacific," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. In cosmetics, French group L'Oréal joined forces with Chinese company Nanomed to develop a Lancome skincare device. Displayed at the 2025 CIIE, the device had reached markets in more than 20 countries and regions by July 2026. In telecommunications, U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm showcased a sixth-generation (6G) communications terminal prototype following tests with China Mobile and Chinese telecommunications equipment maker ZTE. The CIIE also served as a platform for emerging innovators. This year's innovation incubation section featured 633 projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. Taken together, these examples point to an evolution beyond unveiling imported products and technologies. International companies are increasingly developing new technologies and manufacturing innovative products in China, drawing on local expertise to serve both Chinese and overseas markets -- part of what has come to be known as "China Opportunity 2.0." Shanghai's own history offers a wider perspective on this evolution. The city became home to China's first pilot free trade zone in 2013. This July, representatives of 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which will be headquartered in the city. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China next week. The theme of this year's summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," while China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation. In 2025, APEC's 21 member economies were home to 3 billion people and accounted for 61.6 percent of global real GDP. The gathering carries historical resonance. Shanghai hosted APEC leaders in October 2001, just weeks before China's WTO accession, at a meeting that marked a fresh start for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the new century. At the 2014 Beijing summit, leaders endorsed a roadmap toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, an initiative that APEC trade ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing in May. Back in Shanghai, 49 companies and institutions signed up on Nov. 6 for the CIIE's 10th edition in 2027. Among them was German optics group ZEISS, which this year showcased a new-generation intraocular lens developed by its joint venture in China. For Martin Fischer, president and CEO of ZEISS Greater China, China is not only the company's largest market globally, but also a vital source of innovation. "The time it takes to turn an idea into a prototype is shorter in China than anywhere else," he said. (Video reporters: Zhu Cong, Hong Liang, Sun Qing; Video editors: Yang Zeyi, Roger Lott, Zhang Mocheng) ■

item.title: China issues revised regulations on management of foundations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the management of foundations. The revised regulations, which consist of 79 articles in eight chapters, will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. The regulations aim to strengthen the credibility of foundations and promote their sound and orderly development. They stipulate that foundations engaged in public welfare activities must follow the principles of legality, voluntariness, good faith, openness, transparency and non-profit operation. To improve the registration management system, the regulations clarify the registration authority level and registered capital, steadily advance direct registration, specify procedural requirements for registration changes, and refine liquidation procedures prior to deregistration. Highlighting the need to regulate the activities of foundations, these regulations improve requirements for fundraising, donation and grant-making activities, and regulate internet public fundraising and cooperative public fundraising, among others. The regulations also stress the need to improve internal governance, strengthen information disclosure and industry self-regulation, and enhance supervision. ■

item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity. ■
